summary: Build practical workplace mental health support skills with psychosocial risk tools, referral pathways, and action plans. Enquire today.
lede: Workplace mental health awareness and support training helps HR, managers, and other professionals recognize distress and respond appropriately within their roles. It covers spotting signs of stress and burnout, using psychological first aid and trauma-informed support conversations, and identifying psychosocial hazards. Participants also practice mapping referral routes, documenting next steps, and planning workplace wellbeing actions.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who need to recognize mental health concerns early, respond appropriately, and support safer workplace conversations without stepping outside their role.
prerequisites: Prerequisites are an intermediate understanding of workplace operations, HR processes, or people management. No clinical qualification is required, and no coding or programming is required. You should be ready to discuss workplace scenarios, confidentiality boundaries, referral pathways, and psychosocial risk controls. The course is taught at the operational application level, with some conceptual exposure to trauma-informed practice and psychological health and safety frameworks.
